subject: Geopolitics
title: Will Energy Cause the Next War?
description: A 60-second lesson on Will Energy Cause the Next War?.

hook.text: Every great power conflict of the last century involved energy.

buildup.text: The South China Sea holds vast oil and gas reserves. Six nations claim overlapping territory. Navies patrol daily.

discovery.text: Arctic melting opens new routes and resources. Russia, Canada, and the US jockey for control of untapped reserves.

twist.text: Renewables may ease some energy conflicts but spark new ones over mining rights, trade routes, and supply chains.

climax.text: Energy will remain a driver of conflict. The fuels change but competition over power—literal and political—never fades.

punchline.text: The fuel changes. The fight over it stays the same.

quiz.question: Why might energy still cause future conflicts?
options: All nations will soon run out of energy entirely
Competition shifts to new resources, routes, and supply chains
